prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1141; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change on a multi-lane roadway. Insured vehicle reportedly moved into the adjacent lane and contacted the claimant's vehicle on the driver's side. Police report requested. Claimant reports being transported by ambulance with a suspected wrist injury.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from the claimant. Claimant states the other vehicle drifted into their lane without signaling and that contact occurred near the rear quarter panel. Claimant reports pain and swelling in the left wrist and has been advised to keep medical records. Claimant is not represented by an attorney at this time.

Entry 3: Spoke with insured driver. Insured acknowledges the lane change but disputes the degree of fault, stating the claimant was in the blind spot and accelerating. Scene photos requested from insured. Dashcam footage to be checked for relevant timing.

Entry 4: Medical update received from claimant. Diagnosis indicates a fracture of the wrist, with treatment including immobilization and a follow-up appointment scheduled. Claimant asked about the process for submitting medical bills and was provided the general claims guide. No settlement discussion has taken place.

Entry 5: Reviewed police report and dashcam footage. Footage supports the claimant's account that the insured vehicle changed lanes with contact to the claimant's vehicle, though the claimant's speed at the time remains under review. Preliminary liability assessment leans toward the insured. File to remain open pending medical records and final fault determination.
